claim: Saving surge 2021-24 is concentrated where mobile money grew (dev panel)
note: corr sample = 58 countries with MM data in both waves

claim: Resilience change 2021-24 aligns with mobile-money growth (dev panel)
gates: G3 ok, G4 ok, G6 FAIL (0.19 -> -0.005 after drop-top-5)
note: association is a big-country artifact; meaningful negative: MM moved saving (E1) but not resilience

claim: Gender-gap closure 2021-24 aligns with mobile-money growth (dev panel)
effect: r=0.008 (n=59); terciles all ~+0.1pp; d_gap std 7.4pp but orthogonal to MM
note: clean null, verified against join bugs; gap changes are large but MM-unrelated in this window

claim: High usage-intensity 2021 leads account growth 2021-24 (dev panel)
test: weighted corr g20/account ratio vs d_account
note: pre-registered direction rejected; reverse (catch-up) is strong but needs acc-level control -> E5b

claim: Accounts-first pattern: lower 2021 usage-intensity predicts faster 2021-24 account growth at same account level (dev panel)
test: weighted partial corr (ratio vs d_acc | acc21), WLS residualization
gates: G4 ok (77c, 100%), G6 sign-stable but magnitude drops to -0.114 w/o top-5
note: CAVEAT: effect concentrated in large economies; descriptive, not causal

claim: Where formal saving surged, savings became a bigger emergency-funds source (dev panel)
gates: G3 declared (fin24sav), G4 ok (76c, 97.4%), G6 sign-stable (0.54->0.24)
note: links E1+E2: saving surge shifts resilience composition before headline resilience moves

claim: Dormancy J-curve: bigger 2014-17 account drives -> higher 2017 inactivity (dev panel)
effect: r=0.825 (n=77) BUT collapses to 0.014 w/o top-5
gates: G4 ok; G6 sign-check passes mechanically but magnitude collapse = one-country-story per gate intent
note: true as population-weighted statement (India-dominated), not as cross-country regularity; gate-design lesson logged

claim: Income-gap re-widening 2021-24 proportional to poorest-40 jump 2017-21 (dev panel)
gates: G4 ok, G6 n/a at this magnitude
note: clean null: no systematic reversion of the 2021 narrowing

claim: Not enough money (fin11a) barrier among unbanked adults is an income-graded reason, most cited by the poorest (2024 wave)
test: weighted rate of fin11a==1 among account==0, by inc_q
note: single 2024 cross-section, descriptive only; calibration pre-check (not the formal result) picked fin11a as income-sensitive vs fin11b-f

claim: Mobile-only accountholders are younger and less educated than bank-only accountholders (2024 wave)
test: weighted share aged<=35 and share primary-educ-only, mobile-only vs bank-only
note: single 2024 cross-section, descriptive only; consistent with mobile money as on-ramp for underbanked/younger populations
